acceptance_signals: The exact human-admitted task record exists and a create-only task-start baseline is captured before any evidence write, temporary-root allocation, staging, or build.

Every pre-existing changed path is classified: existing scope baselines are preservation-only inputs beneath the included baseline prefix, while prior evidence, prior tasks, driver implementation, automation documentation, and local configuration remain excluded and byte-identical.

Read-only preflight verifies the current distribution-input manifest and both persisted digests, one compatible retained local build backend, the persisted artifact replay driver and evidence-gated short-root APIs, and zero existing task-owned short roots; any deviation stops before allocation.
Exactly one call to run_artifact_replay supplies one injected real action, the current manifest reference, bounded projected paths, and one new normalized repository-relative evidence target.

The injected action receives only the verified short root, stages exactly the current manifest-selected regular files without links, unsafe paths, extras, or byte mismatches, and invokes one offline no-index, no-dependency, no-build-isolation, no-cache wheel build.
The real action is attempted exactly once without retry, repair, alternate backend, dependency installation, or network access and emits exactly one wheel or stops at the first deviation.

Artifact analysis separates managed package and data payload parity from generated metadata and returns one bounded LF-normalized ArtifactEvidence document without host paths, raw output, source contents, credentials, or process identities.

The persisted driver exclusively writes and fsyncs the evidence, computes its exact canonical SHA-256, creates the repository-relative receipt, and calls remove_short_build_root_after_evidence only after receipt creation without stdin or TTY control flow.

Success requires the driver result to report one action attempt, manifest identities, evidence write and revalidation, gated cleanup removal, and exact-root absence; a final read-only zero-root check agrees.

Any manifest, allocation, action, staging, build, artifact, evidence, receipt, or cleanup deviation stops without a second action and does not record cleanup success; a validated root is preserved when evidence has not authorized removal.

STATUS and the dated development log distinguish pre-cleanup immutable evidence from the post-driver cleanup observation, Codex-run validation, unknowns, authority limits, and the next product review without rewriting prior facts.

Only the new task record and baseline, the new dated build-validation evidence, STATUS, and the existing dated development log may change; every product, helper, manifest, schema, test, prior record, prior evidence, local configuration, and other documentation path remains byte-identical.
The declared driver, manifest, short-root, complete Python 3.11, task and repository governance, task JSON, final scope, privacy, zero-root, and diff whitespace checks pass.

No second build, retained background backend, dependency installation, network request, public CLI, installed-package change, external Agent, model, consumer form, credential access, Git mutation, commit, push, publication, release, deployment, scheduling, retry, repair, or full governance journey occurs.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-8e376c9239d14d94afa3ae93f07a6e08 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Perform exactly one bounded offline wheel-build action through the persisted repository-internal run_artifact_replay driver. Before allocation, require the current distribution-input manifest, retained local no-isolation build prerequisites, driver and short-root contracts, zero pre-existing task roots, and a create-only task-start baseline to pass. The injected action receives only the verified short root, stages exactly the manifest-selected regular files, runs exactly one offline no-dependency wheel build without retry or repair, validates managed payload parity, and returns one sanitized ArtifactEvidence document. The persisted driver must exclusively and durably write that new repository-relative evidence, create its receipt, invoke the existing evidence-gated cleanup, and return a privacy-bounded success confirming one action attempt and exact-root absence. Stop at the first deviation and do not modify implementation files or prior evidence.

items: A caller could bypass the persisted driver for evidence or cleanup; the action receives only the short root and the driver must own the evidence target, receipt, cleanup call, and normalized result.
A build or analysis failure after allocation preserves the exact short root and stops the task; cleanup must not be inferred or performed outside the validated evidence gate.
The one permitted real build cannot be retried, repaired, or substituted, even if the first deviation appears locally recoverable.
The action-generated evidence precedes cleanup and therefore cannot itself claim the later cleanup result; STATUS and the dated log own the post-driver observation.
The dirty worktree contains completed driver work and predecessor evidence; broad baseline inclusion grants no authority to alter any predecessor file.
Artifact inspection could leak host paths, raw subprocess output, source contents, or credentials; only counts, canonical digests, booleans, bounded reason codes, and denied authority may persist.
Reviewed assumption: One offline wheel build remains the smallest representative real artifact action.
Reviewed assumption: The retained Python 3.11, pip, and setuptools toolchain can build the current project without network access or dependency installation.
Reviewed assumption: The current manifest checker still reports the same normalized manifest identities before allocation.

Reviewed assumption: The persisted run_artifact_replay, create_short_build_root, create_evidence_receipt, and remove_short_build_root_after_evidence contracts remain unchanged and suitable for the exact replay.
Reviewed assumption: A foreground one-off invocation can call the persisted driver without adding a public CLI or repository implementation file.
Reviewed assumption: The existing dated development log may receive one append-only section while preserving earlier session facts.
Reviewed assumption: A successful driver return is sufficient to attribute evidence writing, receipt creation, and gated cleanup to the persisted caller boundary.
Reviewed unknown: The exact wheel identity and generated metadata identity produced by the one permitted current build.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the current real action completes successfully through the persisted driver on this host.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the real caller needs additional stable observation fields beyond the current privacy-bounded result.

Reviewed unknown: Cross-platform behavior, concurrent adversarial replacement, recovery after failure, future toolchain behavior, repeated reliability, adoption, time savings, causal benefit, and return on investment.
Reviewed unknown: Whether a broader end-to-end governance journey should be proposed after this replay.
